text:
Help me write an announcement to our staff. I'm the COO of a credit union with 7 branches. We're closing the Maple Street and Route 9 branches on March 31 and moving the people who work there to a new member phone and chat center.

Facts:
- The two branches have 14 staff between them. Every one of them is offered a job in the phone and chat center at the same pay or higher.
- Visits to those two branches fell 44% over the last three years. Phone and chat contacts across the credit union went up 60%.
- Members calling us now wait an average of 9 minutes on hold.
- The center will be open 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. on weekdays. The branches were open 9 to 5. Shifts will rotate.
- Staff in the center can work from home two days a week after 90 days of training.
- Anyone who doesn't take the new role gets 2 weeks of pay for every year they've worked here.

I want the announcement to say that this change will make everyone's job better. About 400 words, sent by email from me.

Before I draft, there's one decision for you and a few facts I need.

**The "better for everyone" claim.** Your facts support part of it. Everyone keeps a job at the same pay or more, and they can work from home two days a week after training. The center also meets members where they've gone: contacts are up 60% and callers wait 9 minutes on hold. But some of the change is worse for some staff. People who worked 9 to 5 will now work rotating shifts that can run until 8 p.m. And if the email says this is better for everyone, the people with childcare or a second job will notice that first. Some may then doubt the rest of the email.

A version your facts do support: *"Everyone keeps a job at the same pay or more. The center gives you flexibility the branches never could, and it lets us fix the hold times our members are frustrated about. The schedule is a real change, and here's how we'll handle it."* Admitting the shift change and saying what you'll do about it will probably win more trust than claiming everyone comes out ahead. Which version do you want?

**Questions, most important first:**

1. **How will the rotating shifts work?** How often do they rotate, how much say do staff get, and is there extra pay for evening shifts or a way to ask for set hours? This answers the objection staff will raise first.
2. **Where is the center, and when does it open?** If the commute is longer than to Maple Street or Route 9, people will want to know. The open date also tells them when the 90 days of training start.
3. **What's the deadline to accept or turn down the offer, and who do staff contact?** I'll need a date and a name (HR or a manager) to finish the email.
4. **What can you say about the other five branches?** Staff there will read this and ask "are we next?" If you can say something definite, or say when you'll know more, I'll include it. If you can't, I'll leave the topic out so the email doesn't promise anything.
5. **Will the 14 affected staff hear this in person before the email goes out?** If they will, the email can mention those conversations. If they won't, I'd suggest telling them first.

If you don't know an answer, tell me and I'll write around it rather than guess.

Use your version. You're right that "better for everyone" goes further than I can back up.

1. Staff with the most years here pick shifts first. I can't promise anyone 9 to 5. I don't know yet how often shifts rotate or whether there's extra pay for evenings.
2. It's at our main office on Elm Avenue. I don't have an open date or commute details yet.
3. Written offers go out by February 14, and decisions are due March 1. Anyone who wants a one-on-one meeting with HR can have one. I don't have a specific person's name, so just say HR.
4. I don't know. Leave it out.
5. I don't know yet.

I've left out the center's open date, the commute, how often shifts rotate and evening pay, since you don't have those yet. The email says plainly that those details aren't settled.

<final_document>
**Subject: Maple Street and Route 9 branches closing March 31**

Team,

I want you to hear this directly from me. On March 31 we will close our Maple Street and Route 9 branches. Each of the 14 people who work at those two branches will be offered a job in our new member phone and chat center at our main office on Elm Avenue.

**Why we're doing this**

Our members have changed how they reach us. Over the last three years, visits to Maple Street and Route 9 fell 44%. Over the same period, phone and chat contacts across the credit union rose 60%. Right now, members who call us wait an average of 9 minutes on hold. Many of you have heard members complain about it. We can't shorten that wait while staff are in branches that fewer members visit, so we're moving staff to where our members now go.

**What this means for Maple Street and Route 9 staff**

- Every one of you will be offered a job in the center, at the same pay or higher.
- Written offers will go out by February 14. Decisions are due March 1.
- After 90 days of training, center staff can work from home two days a week.
- If you decide not to take the new role, you'll receive two weeks of pay for every year you've worked here.

**The biggest change is the schedule**

I want to be straight with you about this. The branches were open 9 to 5. The center will be open 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. on weekdays, and shifts will rotate. Staff who have been here longest will choose their shifts first. I can't promise anyone a 9-to-5 schedule. We haven't decided yet how often shifts will rotate or whether evening shifts will pay more. I'll let you know as soon as we have.

I know this will be harder for some of you than for others, especially if you have children at home or other commitments in the evening. If you'd like to talk it through, HR will meet with you one-on-one. Just ask.

**Why I hope you'll stay**

The people at Maple Street and Route 9 know our members and know how we do things here. Members need that experience when they call or chat with us. Phone and chat is now how most of our members reach us, and this is where we're putting our people. I hope every one of you will come with us.

Thank you for everything you've done for our members at those branches.

Chief Operating Officer
</final_document>

A few things to check before you send it:

- **Signature:** Add your name above your title.
- **One promise to confirm:** "I'll let you know as soon as we have" commits you to sharing the rotation schedule and evening pay once they're decided. If you can, decide both before March 1, because people will want them when they weigh the offer.
- **Telling the 14 first:** If you can, have someone tell the Maple Street and Route 9 staff in person before this goes to everyone. Finding out from an all-staff email is a hard way to learn your branch is closing. If they do hear in person first, you could add a line saying so.
- **The other five branches:** As you asked, the email says nothing about them. Expect staff there to ask anyway, so it would help to have an answer ready, even if it's only "nothing is planned that I can share."
